subject.declared_domain: The eight live graph edge types D1 binds a grain to -- FLOWS_TO, READS_FIELD, HAS_FIELD, PROP_PASSES (field grain) and WRITES, READS, WRITES_S3, READS_S3 (artifact grain) -- as a population in the kuzu_nessie_db projection. This card covers that BOUND SET: what it is, where it lives, how much of the live edge space it spans, and how it fails. It does NOT card the D1 rail (wave 1, SC-e-*), the node types (W2-ifqm), or edge DIRECTION (W2-igwg).

methodology.how: ⛔ THIS SUBJECT IS A SELECTION, NOT A THING -- and that is the whole of its methodology. The eight types are not a class the graph knows about; they are the subset of live edge_type values that D1's edge_grain_binding block names and assigns a grain to. The graph itself carries 53 distinct edge_type strings in one CloudEdge REL table with no notion that eight of them are special. So the set COMPOSES live graph edge types and the D1 grain axis, and INVENTS exactly one thing: the binding of each named type to one grain (field or artifact). The selection was made by hand when the D1 block was authored; no code computes it, and nothing re-derives it when new edge types appear in the graph.

composes.note: the single REL table all 53 live edge types share; the eight are a hand-picked subset of its edge_type values
the edge_grain_binding block that names the eight and assigns each a grain

invents.note: the assignment of each named edge type to exactly one grain -- field for FLOWS_TO/READS_FIELD/HAS_FIELD/PROP_PASSES, artifact for WRITES/READS/WRITES_S3/READS_S3

declared_opinions: ONE GRAIN PER TYPE: each edge type is bound to exactly one grain. FLOWS_TO is called field-grain even though 77 of its 961 edges were declared to carry no dstField -- so the binding describes the type's intent, not every instance.

EIGHT OF FIFTY-THREE: the selection is silent about the other 45 live edge types. Their grain is not 'unknown' in any field a consumer can read -- they are simply absent from the binding, which is a different and less visible thing.

PROP_PASSES AND RENDERS ARE EXCLUDED FROM RELATION BINDING BUT NOT FROM GRAIN: the D1 block records both as carrying field-grain flow while being UNMAPPED as relations, so this set includes PROP_PASSES on grain while the relation vocabulary does not admit it.

S3-SPECIFIC TYPES ARE SEPARATE: WRITES_S3 and READS_S3 are bound distinctly from WRITES and READS rather than treated as refinements, so a consumer counting 'writes' must decide whether to sum two types.

⛔ THE BLOCK MIXES GRAINS UNDER AN EDGE-NAMED KEY: `edge_grain_binding` has NINE members, not eight, and the ninth is `S3Key` -- a NODE type, bound under a `partition` grain alongside the eight edge types. A consumer iterating the block to enumerate edge types gets a node type in the result, and the block's own name asserts otherwise. This is the declared-domain problem in miniature: the key says edge, the contents say edge-and-one-node.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: A CLEAN ZERO WITH NO MARKER. Asking this binding for the grain of an unbound edge type returns nothing -- and 'this type has no declared grain', 'this type does not exist', and 'I misspelled the type' are the same answer. The block carries no unknown-grain value and no list of what it excludes, so absence from the binding is the only signal and it is silent.

verdict.why: The bound set is real, exactly resolvable against the live graph, and its key space is clean -- all eight names matched live edge_type values with zero translation, which is a better result than most subjects in this wave. It is genuinely usable for the types it names. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three bounded defects: (1) it binds 8 of 53 live types and is SILENT about the other 45, including CONTAINS which alone is half the entire edge population, so a grain question about most of the graph returns nothing with no marker; (2) two of its eight embedded counts have drifted and the block has no refresh mechanism, while nothing in a branchable field distinguishes stamped counts from live ones; (3) the type-level binding does not hold per-edge -- FLOWS_TO is field-grain by declaration while its own boundary line concedes instances that are not, and that line is itself now stale. Not UNSOUND: the eight bindings resolve, six counts still hold, and a consumer who reads the graph for anything unbound gets correct answers. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked and every scalar is 'measured' -- this is the first card in my set where nothing had to drop below it, because the subject was entirely reachable from this plane. ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION per W2-m-3: omitted, and nothing here is an opinion on this binding's future. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane remediated nothing and edited no carried surface.
